data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy": null, "claim": "The preference is defensible only if we redefine 'rationality' as 'fidelity to the critical method' rather than 'optimization for truth'; the cost is that science becomes a game with arbitrary rules, losing its claim to describe reality, gaining only the coherence of a self-consistent procedure.", "counterconditions": [{"case": "If the critical method can be shown to converge on truth without induction.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}, {"case": "If 'rule-following' inherently implies a belief in the utility of the rules, which reintroduces induction.", "checker_spec": null, "eval": "observation"}], "definitions": [], "derivation": [], "formalization_refs": [], "mechanism": "If we strip away all claims to truth, probability, and verisimilitude, what remains is a set of procedural rules: 'prefer the theory that has survived the toughest attempts to kill it.' This is rational only in the sense of playing a game correctly. It does not connect to the world (no induction), nor does it approximate truth (no verisimilitude). It is a closed loop of criticism. The preference is defensible as 'rule-following,' but the cost is instrumentalism: science no longer tells us about reality, only about the history of our own criticisms.", "premises": [], "schema": "deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1", "scope": {"covers": [], "excludes": ["The preference is defensible only if we redefine 'rationality' as 'fidelity to the critical method' rather than 'optimization for truth'; the cost is that science becomes a game with arbitrary rules,"]}, "simulation_refs": [], "uncertainties": []}
